text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — customer SLA flagged missing audit events for tenant `acme-corp` starting ~09:12 UTC, looks like a surge correlated with the RBAC rollout window. Can people with RBAC/audit context chime in?
Priya Rao: saw alerts. RBAC change deployed at 09:10 that tightened resource visibility; we added a deny-by-default rule for some legacy service accounts.
Maya Chen: hmm. The missing events are admin.* and auth.* for that tenant specifically. Could be emit-side filtering.
Jon Park: Ops alert — queue length on audit-firehose spiked to 18k msgs and the shipper started backpressuring at 09:14. Circuit breaker tripped for one indexer node.
ops-bot: alert: audit-firehose.queue.length > 10k (host=ingest-prod-4) — 09:15 UTC
audit-bot: 237 events dropped (retry exhausted) for tenant=acme-corp between 09:14:05-09:15:20
Omar Vasquez: i'm seeing elevated KMS encrypt latency (p99 ~420ms) for the same timeframe; could explain slower consumer throughput. Any KMS ops/rotation happening?
Priya Rao: no scheduled KMS work. Is it possible RBAC change added extra attributes causing per-event KMS calls? We moved to tenant-scoped key wrap in the last patch.
Maya Chen: correct — we switched to per-tenant key wrapping for audit payloads. For high-volume tenants that increases KMS QPS by factor ~N. We had a limit in front of KMS that should gate that, but maybe it wasn't warmed.
Jon Park: immediate triage steps I suggest: 1) pause per-tenant key wrap for acme-corp (feature flag), 2) backfill dropped events from short-term buffer, 3) increase batching window on shipper to reduce KMS calls. Thoughts?
Priya Rao: agree. addendum: we must validate customer-facing audit events before any backfill — don't want to re-ingest malformed or privacy-sensitive records. Need a quick validation script.
Leah Kim: ping from CS — acme-corp already noticed gaps and is sensitive (compliance reporting). They want an ETA. If we can pause wrap and backfill within 2 hours they might be OK.
Omar Vasquez: I can flip the feature flag and increase shipper batch size from 500 -> 2000 for that tenant. That will reduce KMS calls by ~4x. Will also enable aggressive prefix cache for KV lookups.
Maya Chen: please also add a temporary rate-priority for audit-firehose: route compliance events (admin/auth) to a high-priority lane to avoid being dropped by general QoS. We have an RLS policy field we can use.
Jon Park: implemented QoS reroute for admin/auth for acme-corp at 09:24 UTC. Queue length dropped to 4.1k and consumers recovered.
ops-bot: info: feature-flag "per_tenant_kms_wrap" toggled OFF for tenant=acme-corp by Omar Vasquez at 09:26
audit-bot: replay buffer snapshot created: audit-buffer-09-26-09-15 (size=29k events)
Priya Rao: for backfill validation: propose lightweight checks: 1) schema conformance (v2 audit schema), 2) tenant_id match, 3) redact pii fields per policy, 4) verify signature metadata if present. I can drop a quick Node script.
Maya Chen: good. Keep it strict but fast. We don't need full semantic validation for first backfill, just schema + tenant + redaction. Any event failing should go to quarantine bucket with record for triage.
Omar Vasquez: running a dry-run of batch backfill now against staging validator. Example filter we used: ```jq 'select(.schema=="audit.v2" and .tenant=="acme-corp")' audit_batch.json | ./validate-audit.sh```
Jon Park: also a note on cost: increasing batch size reduces per-event KMS cost but increases memory spikes and indexing batch write IO. For large tenants we should consider compressed NDJSON and per-tenant index rollover.
Priya Rao: security reminder: when we backfill, ensure KMS envelope keys are not leaked into logs. Use masked logging for envelope_id and do not write raw payloads to stdout.
Leah Kim: told acme-corp we'll provide an incident summary and planned reconciliation steps within 90m. They're asking for a CSV of missing event ids post-backfill. Can we produce that?
Maya Chen: yes — backfill job will emit metadata with original_event_id, ingestion_timestamp, validation_status. We'll surface CSV from the reconciliation tool.
Jon Park: follow-up long-term items: - per-tenant ingestion quotas + burst buckets - shard aware indexing for hot tenants - KMS connection pool sizing and per-tenant cached wrapping keys (securely cached in HSM-protected RAM) - better replay sampling to avoid full backfills
Priya Rao: also add an automated schema-canary that samples 1% of events and runs validation pre-ingest, so we fail fast before KMS is invoked.
Omar Vasquez: cost estimate for immediate approach: pausing per-tenant wrap + batching backfill = minimal infra cost (~$200-400 for extra write IOPS). If we keep per-tenant keys but pre-cache wrapping keys, dev effort ~2w but reduces KMS bill by ~30% for heavy tenants.
Maya Chen: thanks all. Action items: Omar toggle flag & run backfill (in 10m), Jon monitor queues and circuit stats, Priya provide validation script and quarantine pipeline, Leah coordinate CS comms. I'll own the incident summary.
Leah Kim: acknowledged, sending update to acme-corp now. :white_check_mark:
Priya Rao: dropping validator gist in #eng-ml shortly.
Maya Chen: closing loop — after backfill completes we'll run reconciliation and post a mini-runbook for this class of incidents (tenant-key-warmup + QoS policies).
Jon Park: noted. Keeping watch.
ops-bot: resolved: audit-firehose.queue.length normalized at 09:40 UTC
Maya Chen: incident closed for now; will follow up with post-incident writeup including cost numbers and schema changes. Thanks everyone. :pray:
